title: Human-readable sizes
hints: Below 1024, print the number as is with " B". Otherwise keep dividing by 1024 and move to the next unit.
Work in float64 so 1536 bytes becomes 1.5. fmt.Sprintf("%.1f %s", v, unit) gives exactly one decimal place.
Stop at TiB even when the number is bigger: 1<<50 bytes is "1024.0 TiB".
